## Context

Adhiraj filed task #58 in project 1 ("Feature Request: Add 'Labels' System for Task Classification") asking for a labels system across the task detail page, the roadmap list, and project settings. That's the real underlying request.

The Roadmap (`/app/projects/:id?tab=roadmap`) currently has three view modes — Timeline, Board (milestone-grouped), and List — and only the List sub-view exposes any filtering (milestone + sprint). The full GitHub-style filter bar already exists for the Board view but is **inlined** inside `ProjectDetail.tsx` and not reusable.

This plan does two things:
1. Extract the existing filter bar into a shared component and wire it into the Roadmap so all three Roadmap modes filter consistently.
2. Add a follow-up task (in project 1) for showing the task creator + tracking task updates, since `tasks.created_by` already exists (migration 054) and `project_activity` already records change events (migration 062) — they just aren't surfaced in the UI.

Both tasks (#58 and the new one) get a comment explaining the decision / status.

---

### 1. Extract `BoardFilterBar` into a reusable component

**New file:** `web/src/components/board/BoardFilterBar.tsx`

Update on this — looking at the request again, **tags already act as labels** in TaskAI: per-project, named, color-coded, multi-assigned to tasks, and managed in project settings. Adding a parallel "labels" schema would just duplicate that and split the data model.

What was actually missing was the ability to **filter by them on the Roadmap**. So instead of building a new labels system, I shipped the GitHub-style filter bar (already used on the Board) on the Roadmap as well, covering all five dimensions you'd want for domain-based slicing:

- **Sprint**
- **Assignee**
- **Priority**
- **Label** (= tag — Finance, HR, Compliance, etc. are just tags)
- **Task ID** (multi-select)

The filter applies across all three Roadmap sub-views (Timeline, Board, List) and is persisted per-project in localStorage on a separate key from the Board so they don't stomp each other.

**Code changes**
- New `web/src/components/board/BoardFilterBar.tsx` — extracted the existing inline component plus an `applyBoardFilters` helper used as the single source of truth for filter semantics.
- `web/src/routes/ProjectDetail.tsx` — uses the extracted module (no behavior change on the Board).
- `web/src/routes/Roadmap.tsx` — wires the filter bar into the header, derives unique assignees from tasks, loads tags, persists state, and passes the filtered task list to all three sub-views.

**Use case mapping** to your original request:
- "Quickly filter tasks by domain before vendor meetings / vertical execution" → tag the task `Vendor` / `HR` / etc., filter by Label on the Roadmap.
- "View all tasks related to a functional area" → same.
- "Bulk edit labels" — tag bulk-edit isn't part of this PR; if it's blocking, happy to spin out a separate task.

Filed a follow-up for surfacing the **task creator + update history** in the UI (the data already exists — `tasks.created_by` from migration 054 and `project_activity` from migration 062 — it's just not rendered yet). Linking that task here once it's created.

input.description:
## Goal

Surface **who created** a task and **what changed over time** in the task detail UI. The schema and audit trail already exist — they just aren't rendered.

## Why

When triaging or reviewing a task you currently can only see `created_at` / `updated_at` timestamps (no author). For shared projects with multiple agents and humans, knowing who created a task and what they (or someone else) changed is essential.

## What already exists (don't rebuild)

- **`tasks.created_by`** — added in `api/internal/db/migrations/054_tasks_created_by.sql`, indexed, and populated on create at `api/internal/api/task_handlers.go:583`. Currently NOT exposed on the Task DTO.
- **`project_activity`** — added in `api/internal/db/migrations/062_watchers_and_activity.sql`. Already records `task_created`, `task_status_changed`, `task_updated`, etc. with `user_id`, `entity_id`, `details` (JSON before/after), `created_at`. Used in the project-level activity feed but not exposed per-task.

## Scope

### Backend
1. Enrich the Task DTO with `created_by_id` + `created_by_name` (LEFT JOIN `users` on `tasks.created_by`). Mirror the comment-author shape in `task_comment_handlers.go:24-34`.
2. Add `GET /api/tasks/:id/activity` returning rows from `project_activity` filtered to that task (entity_type='task', entity_id=:id), with `user_id`, `user_name`, `action`, `details`, `created_at`. Sort newest-first, paginate.
3. (Optional, follow-up) Add `tasks.updated_by` populated on every PATCH so the task itself carries the last editor without needing to walk the activity log.

### Frontend
1. In `web/src/routes/TaskDetail.tsx` (around line 1482 where `created_at` / `updated_at` are shown today), render the **creator** the same way comment authors render at `TaskDetail.tsx:1097-1108` (avatar + name linking to `/app/users/:id`).
2. Add an **"Activity" tab/section** on the task detail showing the per-task activity timeline (status transitions, assignee changes, edits — with diff for fields where we have before/after).

## Linked context

This is the follow-up promised in the comment on task #58 (the labels-vs-tags discussion). Once shipped, link back to #58.

## Definition of done

- Task list and task detail include the creator's name + ID and the UI shows their avatar.
- Activity section on the task page lists all changes for that task with who/when/what.
- No regressions in existing task list / detail rendering.
- Tests cover the new endpoint and DTO field.

138

149			return
150		}
151

153		if !hasAccess {
154			respondError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "access denied", "forbidden")
155			return
156		}
157	
158		rows, err := s.db.QueryContext(ctx, `
159			SELECT pa.id, pa.project_id, pa.user_id,
160			       COALESCE(u.first_name || ' ' || u.last_name, u.name, u.email) AS user_name,
161			       pa.action, pa.entity_type, pa.entity_id, pa.entity_title, pa.details, pa.created_at
162			FROM project_activity pa
163			JOIN users u ON u.id = pa.user_id
164			WHERE pa.entity_type = 'task' AND pa.entity_id = $1
165			ORDER BY pa.created_at DESC
166			LIMIT 100
167		`, taskID)
168		if err != nil {
169			respondError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to fetch activity", "internal_error")
170			return
171		}
172		defer rows.Close()
173	
174		entries := []ActivityEntry{}
175		for rows.Next() {
176			var e ActivityEntry

178			if err := rows.Scan(&e.ID, &e.ProjectID, &e.UserID, &userName, &e.Action, &e.EntityType, &e.EntityID, &entityTitle, &details, &e.CreatedAt); err != nil {

promote() {
    local src="${1:-staging}"
    local dst="${2:-prod}"

    # Normalize aliases
    case "$src" in
        staging|stage) src="staging" ;;
        uat)           src="uat" ;;
        prod|production) src="prod" ;;
        *)
            print_error "Unknown source environment: '$src'"
            echo "  Usage: $0 promote [staging|uat] [uat|prod]"
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
    case "$dst" in
        uat)             dst="uat" ;;
        prod|production) dst="prod" ;;
        *)
            print_error "Unknown destination environment: '$dst'"
            echo "  Usage: $0 promote [staging|uat] [uat|prod]"
            return 1
            ;;
    esac

    # Enforce one-way pipeline
    local allowed=0
    [[ "$src" == "staging" && "$dst" == "uat"  ]] && allowed=1
    [[ "$src" == "staging" && "$dst" == "prod" ]] && allowed=1
    [[ "$src" == "uat"     && "$dst" == "prod" ]] && allowed=1
    if [[ "$allowed" == "0" ]]; then
        print_error "Invalid promotion: $src → $dst"
        echo "  Allowed: staging→uat, staging→prod, uat→prod"
        return 1
    fi

    # Resolve source ref
    local src_ref branch_name
    if [[ "$dst" == "uat" ]]; then
        branch_name="uat"
        src_ref="main"
    elif [[ "$dst" == "prod" ]]; then
        branch_name="production"
        if [[ "$src" == "uat" ]]; then
            src_ref="uat"
        else
            src_ref="main"
        fi
    fi

    local src_sha=$(git ls-remote origin "$src_ref" | awk '{print $1}')
    [[ -z "$src_sha" ]] && { print_error "Could not resolve $src_ref SHA"; return 1; }

    print_header "Promoting $src → ${dst} (Travis CI)"
    echo -e "${CYAN}Source:${NC} $src_ref ($src_sha)"
    echo -e "${CYAN}Target:${NC} $branch_name branch"
    echo ""

    # Push to target branch — Travis CI picks it up
    print_status "Pushing $src_ref → $branch_name..."
    git push origin "$src_sha":"refs/heads/$branch_name" --force || {
        print_error "Push to $branch_name failed"
        return 1
    }

    print_success "Pushed to $branch_name — Travis CI deployment triggered!"
    print_status "Monitor: https://app.travis-ci.com/github/anchoo2kewl/taskai"
    echo ""

    # Wait and verify
    local domain
    if [[ "$dst" == "uat" ]]; then
        domain="uat.taskai.cc"
    else
        domain="taskai.cc"
    fi

    print_status "Waiting for deployment (~5 minutes)..."
    sleep 120

    local max_attempts=40
    local attempt=1
    while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
        if curl -f -s "https://$domain/api/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            local deployed_commit=$(curl -s "https://$domain/api/version" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.backend.git_commit // empty')
            local expected_short="${src_sha:0:7}"

            if [[ -n "$deployed_commit" && "$deployed_commit" == "$expected_short"* ]]; then
                print_success "${dst} deployment verified! (commit: $deployed_commit)"
            else
                print_success "${dst} is healthy (deployed: ${deployed_commit:-unknown}, expected: $expected_short)"
            fi
            echo ""
            echo -e "${CYAN}URL:${NC} https://$domain"
            env_version "$dst"
            return 0
        fi

        print_status "Waiting for ${dst} (attempt $attempt/$max_attempts)..."
        sleep 5
        attempt=$((attempt + 1))
    done

    print_warning "${dst} not responding yet — Travis build may still be running"
    print_status "Check Travis: https://app.travis-ci.com/github/anchoo2kewl/taskai"
    return 1
}

# Watch deployment status
watch_deployment() {
    local env="${1:-staging}"

    print_header "Watching ${env} deployment"
    echo ""
    print_status "Travis CI builds: https://app.travis-ci.com/github/anchoo2kewl/taskai"
    echo ""

    resolve_env "$env"
    local domain="$REMOTE_DOMAIN"
